question: Luxembourg's largest export and import chapters overlap. Which goods does it both sell and buy, is it the same goods going both ways or different goods within the same chapter, and how has this changed from 2005 to 2025?
title: Luxembourg's largest export and import chapters overlap. Whi
name: Goods that go both ways

steps.question: Which product chapters did Luxembourg both export and import most in 2025, and how two-way is the trade in each?
steps.purpose: The largest export and import chapters of the Overview, set side by side.
steps.queried: exports and imports · by HS2 product (top 10) · 2025 · two-way trade index (Grubel-Lloyd)
steps.note: In 2025, Luxembourg's largest overlapping export and import chapters show mostly balanced two-way trade, except Vehicles which are mostly imported.

steps.question: Which product chapters did Luxembourg both export and import most in 2005, and how two-way is the trade in each?
steps.queried: exports and imports · by HS2 product (top 10) · 2005 · two-way trade index (Grubel-Lloyd)
steps.note: In 2005, the same chapters had higher export shares and slightly higher two-way indexes, indicating more balanced trade then.

steps.question: How much of Luxembourg's trade went both ways at chapter level, every five years from 2005 to 2025?
steps.purpose: The two-way share when goods are grouped in chapters.
steps.queried: exports and imports · across all HS2 products · 2005–2025, yearly, every 5 years · two-way trade index (Grubel-Lloyd)
steps.note: Two-way trade at chapter level fell from 74.0% in 2005 to 68.8% in 2025, with some fluctuations.

steps.question: How much of Luxembourg's trade went both ways in the same CN8 product, every five years from 2005 to 2025?
steps.purpose: The two-way share at the finest product detail: the same goods going in and out.
steps.queried: exports and imports · across all CN8 products · 2005–2025, yearly, every 5 years · two-way trade index (Grubel-Lloyd)
steps.note: Two-way trade at the detailed CN8 product level is lower, dropping from 46.5% in 2005 to 39.1% in 2025.

steps.question: Within iron and steel, how two-way is Luxembourg's trade in each heading in 2025: which headings are exported and which imported?
steps.purpose: A chapter that looks balanced: the same goods or different ones?
steps.queried: exports and imports · products 72 · by HS4 product (top 10) · 2025 · two-way trade index (Grubel-Lloyd)
steps.note: Within Iron and steel in 2025, exports and imports focus on different headings with very low two-way indexes, showing one-way flows within the chapter.

steps.question: Which CN8 products did Luxembourg both export and import most in 2025, and how two-way is the trade in each?
steps.purpose: The goods that really go both ways.
steps.queried: exports and imports · by CN8 product (top 10) · 2025 · two-way trade index (Grubel-Lloyd)
steps.note: At CN8 product level in 2025, some large goods like Smartphones are traded both ways in similar amounts, while others like H sections of iron or non-alloy steel are almost only exported.

headline: Luxembourg both exports and imports many of the same product chapters, mostly trading similar goods both ways, but this two-way trade has declined from 2005 to 2025, especially at detailed product levels.

points.text: In 2025, Luxembourg's largest overlapping export and import chapters include Machinery and mechanical appliances, Vehicles and parts, Electrical machinery and equipment, and Plastics, with high two-way trade indexes indicating these goods are traded in similar amounts both ways, except Vehicles which are mostly imported; this pattern was similar in 2005 but with higher export shares and slightly higher two-way indexes, showing a decline in balanced trade over time.

The overall share of Luxembourg's trade that is two-way at the chapter level fell from 74.0% in 2005 to 68.8% in 2025, with fluctuations in between, indicating a modest reduction in balanced trade at this broad product grouping.

At the finest product detail (CN8 level), two-way trade is much lower, dropping from 46.5% in 2005 to 39.1% in 2025, showing that while chapters overlap, the exact same goods are less often traded both ways and this has decreased over time.

Within the Iron and steel chapter in 2025, exports and imports focus on different headings with very low two-way indexes; for example, Steel angles and sections are almost only exported, while Ferrous waste and scrap is almost only imported, demonstrating that balanced trade at chapter level can mask one-way flows in different subcategories.

At detailed CN8 product level in 2025, the largest two-way traded goods include Smartphones for wireless networks and Industrial robots, with high two-way indexes indicating similar export and import amounts, but some large products like H sections of iron or non-alloy steel are almost only exported, confirming that two-way trade varies widely by specific goods within chapters.

conclusion: Luxembourg's largest export and import chapters overlap substantially, and much of this trade is balanced with similar goods going both ways, especially at the chapter level. However, the share of two-way trade has declined from 2005 to 2025, particularly at detailed product levels, reflecting more one-way flows within chapters. This analysis cannot reveal the reasons behind these patterns, and confidentiality masking limits full visibility at detailed product levels.
